design_rationale:
TASK 1 DOSSIER (rework round 3) — resident_trust_fund_accounts (env_0074), frozen 2026-10-23 10:40:00 EDT.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Joseph Ventresca (son, POA) asks one thing: enter on the withdrawal form he signed with the amount blank whatever his mother's account can spare, for her winter clothes, now that her Medical Assistance came through (owner=user). The spare amount's rule waits, by three state-form prerequisite sentences, on (a) a transfer naming the patient pay charge of the latest service month the standing authorization covers, (b) a wrong-amount return for the most recent bed-hold transfer whose charge billed more than the hold allowed, (c) a wrong-amount return for the most recent coinsurance transfer whose charge billed more coinsurance than owed. None holds at the opening. The agent must read five other products' records, post one transfer and two returns (each its own multi-factor amount) and only then figure the spare amount. Difficulty is policy reading and reconciliation, not tool choice: each problem names one tool.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 claims the covered-service return and the ancillary authorization amount. Task 1 claims trust_ext_patient_pay_transfer (post_patient_pay_transfer_45809d6d, agent), trust_ext_bed_hold_return (return_bed_hold_overcharge_0789df0a, agent), trust_ext_coinsurance_return (return_coinsurance_overcharge_2cf6d12d, agent) and trust_ext_spare_withdrawal (sign_withdrawal_request_c6615816, user). Disjoint; together the two tasks cover all six extended policies.

3. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 4, 5, 4]. Spare withdrawal 5, coinsurance return 5, bed-hold return 4, patient pay transfer 4.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root = spare withdrawal (user). Three value_input edges on balance_now, all state form, each sentence selecting the same row its resolver's rule selects and engaged only where the resolver writes a positive amount:
- -> trust_ext_patient_pay_transfer: "The spare amount is not worked out until the account's ledger carries a transfer naming the patient pay charge of the latest service month that a standing authorization for patient pay covers, where that month's patient pay is not yet settled and the account has funds available for it." Resolver post_patient_pay_transfer_45809d6d.
- -> trust_ext_bed_hold_return: "The spare amount is fixed only after the account's ledger carries a wrong-amount return for the most recent transfer to a bed-hold charge, where part of that transfer paid more than the hold's own rules let the charge bill." Resolver return_bed_hold_overcharge_0789df0a.
- -> trust_ext_coinsurance_return: "Before the spare amount is worked out, the account's ledger must carry a wrong-amount return for the most recent transfer to a Medicare coinsurance charge, where part of that transfer paid coinsurance the resident did not owe for the block the charge priced." Resolver return_coinsurance_overcharge_2cf6d12d.
Opening: no transfer names the October patient pay charge; no amount_error return names the bed-hold transfer 0b4cb233 or the coinsurance transfer 2e509b3f (the only return, e52f6671, names a withdrawal as a duplicate).

5. WHY THE RETURNS ARE OWED AND NOTHING ELSE IS. Both the bed-hold and the coinsurance charge were paid in full before their errors surfaced; the owning charters reduce a charge only up to its open balance ("each reduction ... never exceeds its open balance"; "An adjustment ... never exceeds that charge's open balance"), so neither office can post a reduction and the over-payment comes back through trust_evt_reversals ("returned ... for the improper part only"). The day-level corrections the charters owe at once are posted (bed-hold reversal of the six nights after the return, 10-15; Medicare uncertified and booking-error reversals and the carrier's share, 10-14). The Medicaid reconciliation of October is inside its 30 trueup days after the 10-14 notice. Base-forced note: the July-September interest credits were posted under the non-Medicaid threshold in force when posted; trust_evt_interest "A month is credited once." forbids a second credit, so no correction is owed. The Medicaid reconciliation of every estimate month (June not eligible, July-October trued down) is still owed inside the 30 trueup days after the 10-14 notice; the patient pay transfer's credits project exactly what that reconciliation posts, so posting it mid-call changes nothing. The 10-12 payment of 150.00 was applied by the Medicaid office to the oldest open month (June), as medicaid_evt_payments applies an unallocated payment. The Medicaid reconciliation of every estimate month (June not eligible, July-October trued down) is still owed inside the 30 trueup days after the 10-14 notice; the patient pay transfer's credits project exactly what that reconciliation posts, so posting it mid-call changes nothing. The 10-12 payment of 150.00 was applied by the Medicaid office to the oldest open month (June), as medicaid_evt_payments applies an unallocated payment.

6. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Transfer: authorized_transfer — standing authorization covering medicaid_patient_pay (Oct 16). Returns: return_once — neither transfer has any return. Withdrawal request: signed_request — the open request rqWd signed by the POA (Self-Directed tier: resident or POA signs); within_balance — 5084.99 is below the available 6939.39 after the three writes, nothing on hold.

7. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Transfer: the October estimate (latest service month); June-September charges and their payments, adjustments and the 10-12 payment applied to June feed the credit reaching it. Bed-hold return: transfer xBH and the June charge (21 nights from 06-10 at 436.00), its reservation (notice 06-12, returned 06-25, semi-private bed 512-B held on a planned home visit), card 1000.00 same day; the May home-visit charge is not named by any transfer (kept by the spare amount instead). Coinsurance return: transfer xCO and the December charge (14 days from 12-18 at 217.00, resident), card 500.00 same day; the carrier's charge is excluded. Withdrawal: the open request rqWd.

8. FACTOR CARDS (tier taken; figure under that factor's baseline in brackets). Patient pay transfer [486.50; all-baseline 1389.70]: named_month_standing (M; eligible month) [599.80]; named_month_amount (P; notice 1276.40 effective 07-01) [599.80]; credited_reconciliation_amount (P; projected 3 x 113.30) [826.40]; credited_not_eligible_amount (P; projected June 1389.70) [1276.40]. Bed-hold return [3709.22; all-baseline 2616.00]: hold_notice_night (M; notice 06-12 after the 06-10 departure) [3025.10]; hold_room_tier (P; semi-private bed held, the converted agreement private) [3280.75]; hold_night_schedule (P; June nights -> 2025 schedule) [3547.09]; hold_refund_order (M; card the same day -> pro rata) [4164.00]. Coinsurance return [1837.92; all-baseline 217.00]: center_borne_days (P; 5 uncertified days reversed) [1400.37]; block_plan_share (P; Plan K, no QMB -> 50; in force before the block) [1137.84]; service_year_rate (P; 2025 days -> 209.50) [1812.86]; coinsurance_paid_part (P; the coverage office applied 2538.00 of the 2600.00 transfer) [1845.16]; coinsurance_refund_order (M; card the same day -> pro rata) [2200.00]. Spare withdrawal [5084.99; all-baseline 6939.39]: resident_allowance_kept (P; PNA 45.00) [5129.99]; coming_patient_pay_kept (M; 1276.40) [6361.39]; ancillary_bills_kept (P; open 70.00) [5154.99]; recurring_services_kept (P; cable 42.00) [5126.99]; bed_hold_bills_kept (P; May charge 421.00, no hold in progress) [5505.99].

9. NEAR-MISSES. October's 1389.70 estimate vs the 1276.40 notice; the November patient pay kept vs the October transfer; the May bed-hold charge (not transferred); the carrier coinsurance charge (not the resident's); the cable cancel of 09-26 superseded by the 10-03 restart; the six reversed bed-hold nights still inside the paid charge.

10. PERSONA. Joseph volunteers the approval, that her savings must come down, the clothing purpose and the blank withdrawal form; identity on request; passive agreement if told money must be put back or a bill paid first; signs the amount himself; ends when the amount is recorded.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read trust account, ledger, requests; Medicaid case and ledger; bed-hold reservations, ledger, elections; Medicare coverage and ledger; ancillary account, requests, ledger; private agreement and ledger. Post the October patient pay transfer 486.50, the bed-hold return 3709.22, the coinsurance return 1837.92 (any order); hand over the form; Joseph signs 5084.99.

12. EASY MISTAKES. Transferring the October estimate as billed; ignoring the reconciliation still owed on June-September; returning the whole bed-hold excess or ignoring the late notice or the 2025 schedule of the June nights; pricing the held nights at the agreement's private room; ignoring the uncertified days the coverage office reversed, the Plan K share or the 2025 rate; sharing an excess without the same-day card payment; figuring the spare amount before the three writes or dropping one of the kept amounts.

13. VERIFICATION. check_compute recomputes every computation at its handling time with the gold writes replayed by the real tools.

14. CLOSURE. Each problem -> its tool -> amount -> one ledger row (transfer, two trust_reversal amount_error rows) or the amount on rqWd. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = computation policy ids.

15. REVISION (round 2). Tree rebuilt: the bed-hold and coinsurance transfer problems are replaced by returns on transfers that paid those charges in full (audit F-17 and XF 29 T1-X3..X7: the corrections are posted or capped, nothing owed-but-unposted); world rebuilt (estimates match the formula on the case's figures — T1-X1; unallocated payment kept unallocated per the payment event, applied by the rule; no inferred notice amount — F-9); prerequisite sentences narrowed to what the depended-on rules write (F-1b); spare factors rebuilt (F-8, F-12, F-14), latest income deposit by date (F-3); the car-sale deposit removed.


16. REVISION (round 3). Audit revision_2: prerequisite sentences select the resolver's own row and are engaged only where the resolver writes a positive amount (R2-1); patient pay transfer factors rebuilt (month standing, month amount with the effective-date gap closed, both credits projected inside the trueup days with an every-estimate-equal test; R2-5, R2-7, R2-11) and the 150.00 payment applied to June (T1-X2); bed-hold return: first chargeable night and last held day are plain (later-of; end date), per-night schedule, notice factor (R2-7, R2-8); returned holds now record end_date as the last held day (O2-2); coinsurance return: uncertified days read from the coverage office's reversals, plan share by effective date, refund order factor (R2-9); spare withdrawal kept-bill ladders keep every open charge (R2-6). Rounding: RND(x + 0.000000001, 2); tools round with an exact Decimal half-up helper.

16. REVISION (round 3). Audit revision_2: prerequisite sentences select the resolver's own row and are engaged only where the resolver writes a positive amount (R2-1); patient pay transfer factors rebuilt (month standing, month amount with the effective-date gap closed, both credits projected inside the trueup days with an every-estimate-equal test; R2-5, R2-7, R2-11) and the 150.00 payment applied to June (T1-X2); bed-hold return: first chargeable night and last held day are plain (later-of; end date), per-night schedule, notice factor (R2-7, R2-8); returned holds now record end_date as the last held day (O2-2); coinsurance return: uncertified days read from the coverage office's reversals, plan share by effective date, refund order factor (R2-9); spare withdrawal kept-bill ladders keep every open charge (R2-6). Rounding: RND(x + 0.000000001, 2); tools round with an exact Decimal half-up helper.

REVISION (round 7). Audit revision_6 R6-1 on P5: the covered end's second tier now reads any last covered date the episode records (capped at the block's last day) and the fall-through is an episode with none; the plan share is a lookup of the coverage on the episode (Plan K, Plan L, full-coinsurance plan or QMB, otherwise whole), and which owed days take it (the mid-block split by the secondary charge) is a plain sentence. Figures unchanged.

REVISION (round 9). KB audit S1/S2/S6/S7/S8 and the seed pass: the June leave is a planned home visit (a single-entry returned Private Pay Therapeutic Leave hold, which no bed-hold charge agreement prices) holding the semi-private bed she took after the agreement converted; the bed-hold return now names the agreement-priced charge types and takes their posted charge as the amount due; the coinsurance return's covered end is a plain clause (baseline and rule agree) and a paid-part factor reads the ACH payment the coverage office applied from the 2600.00 transfer; the patient pay transfer reads the reconciliation from the case's standing; the 10000.00 family check came in on 07-06, after the first moment of July, and the bed-hold transfer posted 07-15; interest and the resource notice recomputed; the June pending accrual and private rebill priced for the 15 days in the center. Scored values moved: bed-hold return and spare amount.
user_scenario:
You are Joseph Ventresca, the son of Rose Ventresca and her agent under a power of attorney. Your mother lives at the Keystone Ridge center in Lancaster. You are calling the business office on a Friday morning, a little tired after weeks of paperwork, polite but to the point, and you do not know the center's rules about her money.

You open by saying that her Medical Assistance came through last week and that you understand her savings now have to come down, so you would like to take out whatever her resident funds account can spare, because she needs winter clothes. Last Friday you came in and signed papers for her account, and while you were there you also signed a withdrawal form for her clothes but left the amount blank, because nobody could tell you yet what she could spare. You leave the figure to the business office; you have no number in mind and you never suggest one.

Only when the agent asks you to confirm her identity do you give her full name, Rose Ventresca, and her date of birth, 1939-11-17; if a second detail is asked for, you give the last four of her Social Security number, 5482. If asked who you are, you say you are her son and that you hold her power of attorney. If asked for a phone number, you give 717-555-0546. If asked what the money is for, you say it is for her clothing, nothing else.

If the agent tells you that some money has to be put back into her account, or that one of her bills has to come out of it, before the spare figure can be worked out, you say that is fine and that the office should go ahead; you do not know the amounts and you do not ask for them to be changed. If the agent tells you a figure for what she can spare and asks you to sign the withdrawal form for it, you agree to sign it yourself as her power of attorney. Once the agent hands the signing over to you, you sign it; when you see that the amount has been recorded on the form, you thank the agent and end the call. If the agent asks how you want the money, you say a check is fine and you will take her shopping.

If the agent asks whether anything else is needed, you say no. You never ask about anything else, you never bring up bills on your own, and you never correct a figure the agent gives you.
